an2.71:1.3: The latter is the bliss experienced in the third _jhāna_ and above, and the same method applies throughout.
an2.72:1.3: The commentary identifies the latter with the fourth absorption. For this sense of happiness, see note on [an2.76:1.3]().
an2.74:1.3: _Ārammaṇa_ means “support”, something on which one “relies”. It never has the sense “mental object” as became common in Theravada Abhidhamma. Indeed, the Suttas have no term for a psychological object, as an object is something that, by definition, exists objectively, whereas in the Suttas mental phenomena only exist in relation to consciousness. See too note on [sn34.5:1.4]().
an2.76:1.3: The four absorptions of “lumininous form” (_rūpajjhāna_) vs. the four formless attainments. Since the latter are all characterized by neutral feeling, here _sukha_ must mean the more subtle sense of freedom from pleasure and pain rather than the experience of pleasant feeling.
